newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: LUKoil in talks with Azeris on new oilfield.
newsitem.headline: LUKoil in talks with Azeris on new oilfield.

text.p: Russia's largest oil producer, NK LUKoil, held talks with Azeri officials on Friday on tapping the Inam oilfield in the Azeri sector of the Caspian Sea.

LUKoil vice-president Ravil Maganov said LUKoil wanted a 50 percent stake in the $2 billion project to develop the field, which he said had estimated reserves of 120-150 million tonnes (880 million to one billion barrels).
LUKoil officials met counterparts from the Azeri state oil company SOCAR to discuss the field, near the Shakh-Deniz structure.
Maganov said it was possible SOCAR could bring on board Western oil companies for the project.
He said LUKoil might finance its participation through its joint ventures LUKArco, which is with Atlantic Richfield Company of the U.S., or through LUKAgip, a venture with Agip SpA of Italy.

LUKoil is already part of three international, multi-billion- dollar offshore projects in Azerbaijan -- it has a 10 percent stake in the $8 billion Azerbaijan International Operating Company, a 10 percent stake in Shakh-Deniz and a 12.5 percent stake in Karabakh. The LUKAgip joint venture owns 45 percent of Karabakh.
